title: Fake help desk on Teams to domain admin via AD CS: Microsoft details ESC1 and ESC8 intrusions
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence described two intrusions that started with external Teams chats and calls impersonating IT support, followed by a user-approved Quick Assist session that dropped portable Python, Bun or Java runtimes into a KB-named folder under AppData. In one case the attacker abused an ESC1-vulnerable template to get certificates for 11 privileged accounts and ran DCSync; one account excluded from automatic attack disruption was then used to exfiltrate file-server data with a renamed Rclone. In the other, PetitPotam coerced a domain controller into NTLM that was relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8), and the resulting DC certificate was used for PKINIT. No Teams vulnerability was involved.
why: The chain needs no malware attachment and no CVE: just one user saying yes to a 'support' call and one weak template or an NTLM-enabled /certsrv endpoint. A certificate survives password resets and reimaging, so incident response has to revoke certificates and deal with issued Kerberos tickets as separate steps.
todo: Run Locksmith or Certipy (find) against your CAs and fix any ESC1 template (enrollee supplies subject plus client authentication EKU plus broad enrollment rights) and any ESC8 exposure: remove Web Enrollment if unused, otherwise require HTTPS with Extended Protection for Authentication and disable NTLM per KB5005413.
Restrict Teams external access to allowed domains and make sure users see External and suspected-scam labels; set a rule that IT never starts Quick Assist from an inbound call.

Block or audit portable runtimes (bun.exe, java.exe, python.exe) launched from user-writable paths with App Control for Business, and hunt with the KQL in Microsoft's post (KB-prefixed AppData folders, connections to 88/445/636).
Review exclusions from Defender automatic attack disruption: in Case 1 the one excluded privileged account was the one that led to data theft.
Turn on Certification Services auditing (success and failure) and the CA audit filter so you can find the serial number of any rogue certificate to revoke.
